# @favy/di

> Documentation for the current @favy/di source, a lightweight dependency injection library for TypeScript.

Canonical documentation: https://di.favy.dev/
Source: https://github.com/favyorg/di

## Start Here

- Introduction: https://di.favy.dev/guides/introduction/
- Core Module model: https://di.favy.dev/module/module/
- Caching: https://di.favy.dev/module/cache/
- Lazy initialization: https://di.favy.dev/module/lazy/
- Partial application: https://di.favy.dev/module/partial/
- Testing: https://di.favy.dev/guides/testing/
- Best practices: https://di.favy.dev/guides/best-practices/
- Transform input: https://di.favy.dev/module/transform-input/
- Transform output: https://di.favy.dev/module/transform-output/
- API reference: https://di.favy.dev/reference/api/

## Installation

```bash
npm install @favy/di
```

The declarations require TypeScript 5.0 or newer.

## Typed Quick Start

```typescript
import { Module, type Live } from '@favy/di';

const Logger = Module()('Logger', () => ({
  log: (message: string) => console.log(message),
}));
type LoggerLive = Live<typeof Logger>;

const App = Module<LoggerLive>()('App', ({ Logger }) => ({
  start: () => Logger.log('Application started'),
}));

App({ Logger }).start();
```

`Live<T>` combines the dependencies required by a module with the value that module provides under its name. A top-level module call supplies module implementations and dependency values. Module implementations are resolved through the graph.

Dependency contracts describe object maps. Runtime maps passed to module calls or `.provide()` may be any non-null object, including class instances and custom-prototype objects; only their own string and symbol keys are consumed. Discriminated unions retain their branch-specific required fields. The default factory supplies generated `{ Module: { name } }` invocation metadata; use `ModuleLive` when a callback needs it.

A provider's remaining dependencies must appear in the matching branch of the consumer's declared dependency context. Use `Live<typeof Provider>` to carry those transitive requirements; a module requiring extra fields cannot be inserted into a result-only dependency slot and turned into an unsafe zero-argument callable. Discriminated-union calls and partials may use a branch-specific provider once their discriminant selects the branch that contains its requirements.

## Partial Application

```typescript
import { Module } from '@favy/di';

const Add = Module<{ left: number; right: number }>()(
  'Add',
  ({ left, right }) => left + right,
);

const AddTen = Add.provide({ left: 10 });
AddTen({ right: 5 }); // 15
```

`.provide()` tracks the supplied keys and updates the returned callable's remaining dependency type. Bound values take precedence over the same keys in a wider root object.

## Lazy Dependencies

The default `lazy: true` initializes a module dependency only when its property is accessed. Avoid destructuring a dependency before a conditional access. Object rest/spread enumerates the context and reads every included provider.

```typescript
import { Module, type Live } from '@favy/di';

const Expensive = Module()('Expensive', () => ({
  value: 42,
}));
type ExpensiveLive = Live<typeof Expensive>;

const Consumer = Module<ExpensiveLive>()('Consumer', ($) => ({
  read: (enabled: boolean) => (enabled ? $.Expensive.value : 0),
}));

Consumer({ Expensive }).read(false); // Expensive is not initialized
```

## Custom Module Factories

```typescript
import { makeModule } from '@favy/di';

const SingletonModule = makeModule({
  cache: 'module',
  lazy: true,
});

const Connection = SingletonModule()('Connection', () => ({
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
}));

Connection();
SingletonModule.flushCache();
```

Cache modes:

- `run` (default): reuse a dependency during one top-level call.
- `module`: reuse values for the lifetime of that `makeModule` factory, until `flushCache()`.
- `none`: recompute whenever a module dependency is accessed.

An ordinary `transformInput<D, PD>` has the preserving signature `<DX extends D>(deps: DX, name) => DX & PD`; TypeScript rejects transforms that drop input fields and requires the caller-supplied portion of every later module dependency map to satisfy `D`. Constrained preserving transforms can be written inline as `<DX extends Base>` or assigned an explicit `transformInput<Base, Added>` type. Fields explicitly required by `Base` remain caller-supplied because the transform receives that input before it adds callback values. Use an `HKT` when replacing the callback shape; an input HKT receives the declared module key in `_NAME` and the dependency map in `_RESULT` and `_DEPS`. The HKT marker is nominal, so an ordinary `_NAME` field does not activate it. Custom metadata keeps its declared `name` type unless the transform returns `withModuleName(...)`.

Omitting transforms in `makeModule({})` uses typed defaults: generated `Module.name` input and identity output. A custom ordinary `transformOutput<I, D, O>` constrains callback results to `I` and makes module callables return `O`; a generic identity output preserves each callback result. Use an output HKT when the callable type must be computed from the module name, result, or dependencies.

## Public Exports

```typescript
import {
  Module,
  makeModule,
  withModuleName,
  type DefaultModuleFactory,
  type HKT,
  type Kind,
  type Live,
  type MakeOptions,
  type ModuleLive,
  type TModule,
  type transformInput,
  type transformOutput,
} from '@favy/di';
```

Use the API reference for signatures and the focused guides for lifecycle and transformation semantics.
